posts.name: The Girl With No Name
posts.cooked:
I hope this is the right place to post a story about a game I just played. 

 

Citizen Dawn against Expat, Setback, Parse and Ra (all base). I was Parse. Everyone's set up and ready to go when Devastating Aurora shows up. No biggie, I say to the group. Parse has a Buffer Overflow in play, so I can say "see ya!" to the Aurora! Aurora gets discarded, Buffer blows up, Parse draws, and the next card is played. 

 

It's the other Devastating Aurora. 

 

Personally, I blame Setback. I don't know what he did, but I'm sure he's responsible in some way.

posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
Yeah, Parse is mostly OP but she still has her limits. It's particularly annoying when Extrasensory Awareness turns up all three cards that are all terrible, because unlike most deck control it doesn't dump one of the cards to the bottom. The best you can do is shuffle and pray the other two don't show up after all.

In non-Dawn shenangians, I'm reminded of a recent F5 variants vs Ultimate Voss game where he played Forced Deployment three turns in a row... while Sub-Zero Atmosphere was out (meaning it would always get destroyed right after it was played). I managed to always survive the onslaught and throw everyone back into the trash again (and did win in the end), but, ouch.

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
Yeah, against Dawn and other villains (like Omitron) that have one card that's just way more awful than anything else they have, I work really hard to get out two "counterspells" (as we call them).  The double play happens way more often that chance would seem to suggest.

Jeysie:

In non-Dawn shenangians, I'm reminded of a recent F5 variants vs Ultimate Voss game where he played Forced Deployment three turns in a row… while Sub-Zero Atmosphere was out (meaning it would always get destroyed right after it was played).

Wait, why would that happen?  Forced Deployment goes off at the start of the turn.  Sub-Zero Atmosphere doesn't do anything to cards that go off at the start, only ones that go off at the end.  That should only happen if there's an environment that plays villain cards (like Slamara).
